prompt:
A German woman in her fifties stands on the grey stone pavement of a Berlin
street corner, seen from the waist up, three quarters turned to her left,
right of centre in a vertical frame. A dark navy wool coat over a white top,
a cream tote bag hanging from her forearm, her hair tied back. Her face is
indignant and polite at once, and she looks at a point beyond the left edge
of the frame, away from the camera.

The bottom edge of the picture crosses her coat just below the tote bag, and
the top of her head sits a hand's width under the top edge, so that her face
is one of the largest things in the picture.

She stands on worn pale grey stone slabs. Behind her coat a straight granite
kerb, a plain pale stone lip, crosses the picture horizontally, and past that
kerb, higher in the frame and further from the camera, a red asphalt lane runs
across and away to the right, with the grey asphalt of the road past it.

Close beside her, level with her head, a pedestrian traffic light stands on a
bare grey pole, its black housing holding two round lenses, the upper one lit
and glowing an even plain red. Behind her the pavement runs on with parked
bicycles along a plain pale building front. Daylight, overcast and flat.
